title: Hydrochloric Acid-Potassium Chloride Buffer Preparation
author: Neilier Junior
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfycjpsw

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 M KCl solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 7.45 g potassium chloride (MW 74.5 g mol⁻¹) in deionized water and dilute to a final volume of 1 L to obtain a 0.1 M KCl solution (pH range 1–2.2).

steps.title: Mix KCl and HCl
steps.instruction: Pipette 50 mL of the 0.1 M KCl solution into a beaker, add the indicated volume of 0.1 M hydrochloric acid required for the desired pH, then bring the total volume to 100 mL with deionized water.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 mL of 0.1 M KCl solution.
Add the calculated volume of 0.1 M HCl.
Adjust volume to 100 mL with deionized water.

steps.title: Adjust final pH
steps.instruction: Measure the pH with a calibrated sensitive pH meter and, if needed, fine‑tune the pH to the target range (pH 1–2.2) by adding small amounts of 0.1 M HCl or deionized water.
